summary: Add visual models and varied exam practice for bounded area and trapezium estimates.

improvements.where: note, after the bounded-area paragraph in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: P2-8.2 asks learners to identify the upper curve and the bounded region; the diagram gate requires a figure.
improvements.what: Add a graph_sketch of $y=6x-x^2$ and $y=2x$ on $0\leq x\leq4$, with intersections labelled and the enclosed region shaded; request it in pack diagrams and embed the generated SVG in the note.

improvements.where: note, after the trapezium-rule formula in ## Key ideas
improvements.why: P2-8.3 is easier to understand when the shared interior ordinates and straight trapezium edges are visible.
improvements.what: Add a graph_sketch of $y=x^2$ on $[0,2]$ with two trapezia, labelled width $h$ and the middle ordinate; show that the straight edges lie above the curve. Request and embed the generated SVG.

improvements.why: All existing numerical trapezium items repeat $x^2$ on $[0,2]$, whereas Pearson specifies a radical example and possible error estimates.
improvements.what: Add an exam-style four-strip estimate for $\int_0^1\sqrt{2x+1}\,dx$ with a table of five ordinates, and a linked error question comparing with the exact integral; use Calculate/Show that and full working.

improvements.why: Current bounded-area items all use a quadratic and line meeting at zero and one positive value, so they never test splitting when curves cross within the requested interval.
improvements.what: Add a structured area question on a stated interval where the upper curve changes at an interior intersection; require the learner to split the integral and add positive areas.

improvements.why: The library advises repeating the area calculation for each region and adding, while the current worked example covers only one region.
improvements.what: Add a brief two-region worked demonstration: find every crossing, determine the upper curve separately on each interval, integrate each positive difference, then add the areas. Paraphrase the library method.
